title: Python: Storing a Word
description:
A variable is a box that holds a value.
You give the box a name. You put something in it.

    name = "Alex"

Output:

The = sign means "store this value in this box."
It does NOT mean "equals" like in math.

title: Python: Basic Math
description:
Python can do math for you.

    print(5 + 3)    # Output: 8
    print(10 - 4)   # Output: 6
    print(3 * 4)    # Output: 12
    print(10 / 2)   # Output: 5.0

The symbols:
  +  means add
  -  means subtract
  *  means multiply
  /  means divide

(# is a comment — Python ignores it, it's just a note for you.)

title: Python: Asking a Question
description:

input() pauses and waits. It stores what the user types.
The + joins two pieces of text together.

title: Python: Making a Decision
description:
if lets your program choose what to do.

    temperature = 90

    if temperature > 80:
        print("It's hot outside!")

The code inside if only runs when the condition is true.
Notice the colon : at the end of the if line.
Notice the 4-space indent before print.

title: Python: Two Paths (if/else)
description:
else gives your program a second path — what to do when the if is NOT true.

    score = 45

    if score >= 60:
        print("You passed!")
    else:
        print("Try again.")

Output:
    Try again.

If score was 75, it would print "You passed!" instead.
if handles one case. else handles everything else.

title: Python: Counting with a Loop
description:
A for loop repeats code a set number of times.

    for i in range(5):
        print(i)

Output:
    0
    1
    2
    3
    4

range(5) gives you the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
It starts at 0. It stops before 5.
i is a variable that changes each time through the loop.

title: Python: Your First Function
description:
A function is a block of code you write once and use many times.

    def say_hello():
        print("Hello there!")

    say_hello()
    say_hello()

Output:
    Hello there!
    Hello there!

def means "define a new function."
The function name is say_hello.
The () means it takes no input.
You call it by writing say_hello() — the () is how you run it.

title: Python: Functions with Input

You pass values in when you call the function: greet("Sam").

title: JavaScript: const and let
description:
In JavaScript, you use const or let to create variables.

    const name = "Alex";     // const: value never changes
    let score = 0;           // let: value can change later

    score = score + 10;
    console.log(score);      // Output: 10

Rule of thumb:
Use const by default.
Use let only if you need to change the value later.

title: JavaScript: for Loops
description:
A for loop in JavaScript has 3 parts:

    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      console.log(i);
    }

Output:
    0
    1
    2
    3
    4

Breaking it down:
  let i = 0   → start i at 0
  i < 5       → keep going while i is less than 5
  i++         → add 1 to i each time (same as i = i + 1)

title: JavaScript: Arrays
description:

    const colors = ["red", "green", "blue"];

    console.log(colors[2]);   // Output: blue

Arrays start counting at 0, not 1.
So the first item is at position [0].
